title: PVR INOX Posts Record Quarter as India Box Office Crosses Rs 4,000 Crore
headline: PVR INOX Posts Record Quarter as India Box Office Crosses Rs 4,000 Crore
subheadline: India's gross box office reached Rs 4,443 crore in July-September, the first quarter above Rs 4,000 crore, as PVR INOX profit more than doubled to Rs 273 crore.
summary: India's gross box office reached Rs 4,443 crore in July-September, the first quarter above Rs 4,000 crore, as PVR INOX profit more than doubled to Rs 273 crore.
excerpt: India's gross box office reached Rs 4,443 crore in July-September, the first quarter above Rs 4,000 crore, as PVR INOX profit more than doubled to Rs 273 crore.
body:
• PVR INOX reported its highest-ever quarterly revenue of Rs 2,133 crore in Q2 FY27, up 17% year on year, with profit after tax up 111% to Rs 273.3 crore.
  • India's gross box office collections reached Rs 4,443 crore in the quarter, up 23% — the first time the market has crossed Rs 4,000 crore in a single quarter, according to Ormax Media estimates cited by the company.
  • Growth came from spending per visit, not footfall: admissions rose only 4% to 46.3 million, while average ticket price and food-and-beverage spend each rose 14%, to Rs 298 and Rs 153.
  • English-language films were the fastest-growing segment, up 87% to Rs 1,024 crore, led by Spider-Man: Brand New Day at Rs 608 crore.

PVR INOX has reported the strongest quarter in its history, with revenue, operating profit and net profit all at record levels for the three months ended September 30, 2026. The results, announced on October 28, came as India's theatrical market crossed a threshold it had never reached before: Rs 4,443 crore in gross box office collections in a single quarter, according to Ormax Media and company estimates cited in the company's results announcement.

Records across the board

On an Ind AS 116-adjusted basis, PVR INOX revenue rose 17% to Rs 21,327 million (about Rs 2,133 crore). Adjusted EBITDA rose 44% to Rs 4,752 million, with the margin widening to 22.3% from 18.1% a year earlier. Profit after tax from continuing operations rose 111% to Rs 2,733 million, from Rs 1,296 million in the same quarter last year. First-half revenue reached Rs 37,750 million, up 15%, with first-half profit up 233% to Rs 3,438 million.

"Q2 FY'27 has been a landmark quarter for Indian cinema and PVR INOX. We achieved record quarterly and half-yearly revenue, EBITDA and PAT, supported by strong content, higher consumer spends and disciplined costs."

— Ajay Bijli, Managing Director, PVR INOX

Spend per head did the work

The chain welcomed 46.3 million patrons, only 4% more than a year earlier, and occupancy improved to 30.4% from 28.7%. Revenue grew much faster than admissions because each visit was worth more: the average ticket price rose 14% to Rs 298 and average food and beverage spending per head rose 14% to Rs 153. Ticketing and food-and-beverage revenues each grew 18%.

Hollywood led, Hindi and regional followed

English-language films recorded the sharpest growth, with collections up 87% to Rs 1,024 crore — the first time that segment has crossed Rs 1,000 crore in a quarter. Spider-Man: Brand New Day became the highest-grossing English film in India at Rs 608 crore, and Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey added Rs 233 crore. The Avengers: Endgame re-release, Avengers: Endgame Encore, earned Rs 45 crore in four weeks. Hindi collections, including dubbed films, grew 12%, led by Hanuman Ansh at Rs 351 crore and Mirzapur: The Movie at Rs 267 crore. Regional collections also grew 12%, led by Toxic (Kannada) at Rs 296 crore and Jana Nayagan (Tamil) at Rs 199 crore. First-half industry collections stood at Rs 7,618 crore, up 22%.

Cash, buyback and screens

The company generated Rs 6,035 million in free cash flow in the first half and repaid Rs 2,586 million of debt. It completed its first share buyback, worth Rs 3,000 million, in September and still ended the quarter net cash positive at Rs 1,407 million, up from Rs 807 million at the end of June. A new capital allocation policy targets returning about 30% of annual surplus cash flow through dividends or buybacks and keeping net debt at no more than 0.5 times trailing EBITDA after distributions. PVR INOX operated 1,797 screens across 114 cities in India and Sri Lanka at September 30. It opened 24 screens and exited 25, largely loss-making sites, in the first half, and plans 90 to 100 new screens in FY27, mostly in the second half and through capital-light models. Its first SMART Cinema, a format for smaller Tier III and Tier IV markets, opened in Muzaffarpur, Bihar, in September, with two to three more planned this year.

What comes next

The slate the company is counting on for the second half includes Ramayana: Part One in November, Shah Rukh Khan's King in December, and Love & War and Golmaal 5 in the fourth quarter, alongside Chiranjeevi's Kaaka and Prabhas's Spirit, and Hollywood releases including The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping, Avengers: Doomsday and Dune: Part Three. For diaspora audiences, the quarter's mix is the story: franchise Hollywood, Hindi tentpoles and regional hits all grew at once, which is what pushed the market past Rs 4,000 crore for the first time. Full reported figures are in the coverage by Bollywood Hungama.
